Question B-003-012-006.

Why the correct answer is right: Removing the carrier in a double-sideband voice signal lets more transmitter output be used for the information-bearing sidebands.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "More of the output power can be put into the sidebands": This is the correct choice because removing the carrier in a double-sideband voice signal lets more transmitter output be used for the information-bearing sidebands.
- sourceIndex 1: "Only half the bandwidth is needed for the same information content": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from More of the output power can be put into the sidebands. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Greater modulation percentage is obtainable with lower distortion": This answer would fit a different fault than More of the output power can be put into the sidebands. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, reducing that quantity is not the mechanism that produces the correct effect here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Simpler equipment can be used to receive a double sideband suppressed carrier signal": This option confuses another station topic with More of the output power can be put into the sidebands. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, carrier terminology is being applied to the wrong modulation condition here.
